notes: The sequence, from the source doc: the domain declaration creates the BOUNDARY; Track 2 creates the OBJECT inside it; readiness ASSESSES that object; freeze RATIFIES it.
`assessability` (ASSESSED | DOMAIN_UNPOPULATED) is the mechanism that keeps "nothing to assess" distinguishable from "assessed and failing".
`verifiedFailingBeforeFix` recorded as false: the source docs do not record a fail-before/pass-after run for this canary. Not assumed.

canaries.assertion: `domainAcceptsAssignment()` reads ratification status rather than assuming one and still refuses when unratified; eligibility is locked to `validated|canonical` and rejects `proposed`; the vP1 namespace boundary and its ruled exclusions are pinned against their duplicate in scripts/export-crystal-snapshot.mjs.

statement: Declaring a domain boundary, constituting the object inside it, assessing that object and freezing it are four distinct governed acts and may not be collapsed into one.

occurrences.defect: Readiness was run before crystal constitution had occurred, so nine checks correctly declining to certify an empty set read as nine defects in Crystal vP1. Separately, a caller-supplied domain won over the ratified declaration, so every readiness report the panel requested was about the historical namespace.
